This is a cosmetic variant of the archived "R&D-Adjusted Loss Liability Spiral" — identical R&D leg and identical NEG((pi+xrd)/at) addback term with only the second distress component swapped from liability growth to cash-balance change — so it tests essentially the same mechanism already documented.

Debt maturity structure ((dltt−dlc)/lt) is a genuinely new second leg relative to the archive's level-based leverage and net-debt legs, the duration-matching rationale for long-lived R&D assets is economically coherent, and the expression's direction cleanly matches the positive expected sign.

It is effectively the sign-flipped recombination of two archived signals ("Intangible Sales-Efficiency Runway" and "Intangible Cash-Burn Leverage Trap"), and the sale/intan term is numerically unstable for firms with tiny intangible balances, so the sort will be driven by scaling outliers rather than the stranded-asset mechanism.

This is a near-mechanical substitution into the archived "Goodwill Margin-Erosion Debt Overhang" (same gdwl/at × SUMRANK(distress, lt/at) template) with a low-tax leg borrowed from other archived signals, and low txt/at is largely a proxy for low profitability, making the composite close to a trivial goodwill-times-low-profitability-times-leverage screen.

The contrarian pairing of tax-validated current profitability with a *level* accumulated-deficit (rather than the archived delta-RE version) is internally consistent and economically motivated, though it sits uncomfortably close to the already-tested "Tax-Paying R&D Solvency" and "R&D No-Tax Deficit Drift" and risks being dominated by the well-known negative RE/at distress effect.
